headline: Ethics and timeline cloud Jamaat MP’s marriage claim
summary: Questions arise regarding the timing and ethical implications of a Member of Parliament from Jamaat-e-Islami
details: A Member of Parliament from Jamaat-e-Islami has faced scrutiny over claims regarding his marriage.
The controversy centers on the timeline of events and the ethical considerations surrounding the claim.
Observers and critics have raised questions about the authenticity and timing of the marriage claim.
The situation has sparked a wider debate on the accountability and ethics of elected officials.

headline_marked: ICT judges [[likely to inspect Aynaghar sites]] in Dhaka
headline: ICT judges likely to inspect Aynaghar sites in Dhaka
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 may visit alleged secret detention centers where victims of enforced disappearances were reportedly held and tortured.
details: Judges of the International Crimes Tribunal-1 (ICT-1) are expected to visit two alleged secret detention centers in Dhaka, known as 'Aynaghar'.
The sites include the Joint Interrogation Cell at Kochukhet, reportedly operated by the DGFI, and the Task Force for Interrogation (TFI) Cell at the RAB-1 headquarters in Uttara.
The inspection is linked to ongoing crimes against humanity cases involving deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed.
ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam urged the visit, citing precedents from the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia for ensuring fair trials.

In a separate development, the prosecution has urged the tribunal to frame charges against former lawmaker Mohammad Habib Hasan and 24 others for the killing of 11 people during the July uprising in Uttara.
The charges include the killing of BUP student Mir Mahfuzur Rahman Mugdho and the alleged killing of Mokhlesur Rahman Durjoy, whose body was reportedly dumped in the Turag River.
Additionally, the tribunal is considering charges against Sheikh Hasina and others regarding the alleged killing of nine youths in a staged anti-militancy operation at Kalyanpur’s Jahajbari.
The tribunal has scheduled August 2 for hearing the defense's discharge petitions.
caption:
